answer.evidence: The chair is drawn lying on its side as a flat profile shaped like a T or C. The silhouette widths are 16 (rows 3-4), 5 (rows 7-9) and 11 (rows 11-12). The seat at rows 2-6 is a uniform blue band with no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse, so it shows no horizontal surface seen from above. The vertical blue bar at rows 5-12 is the backrest and is exempt. The grey strips at rows 3-4 and 11-12 are legs seen in side profile. There is no top surface and no receding side face, so it reads as a profile silhouette without a top, like the 'side elevation chair' reference.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny blue glyph-like shape, about 14x12 px, with only 10 distinct colours. It reads as a fallen chair only vaguely, if at all. It has about 2-3 flat tones with a light outline and no visible grain, highlights or per-part shading. Beodeul props such as the bench, well and stall show 5-6 steps per material, tinted dark outlines, and wood grain or tile and stone texture. The tile-based measures (0 tones per tile) don't apply because the piece is smaller than a tile, so I judged by eye. By eye it is much thinner and flatter than the bench, the nearest reference in kind, which has slat highlights, shadow and leg detail. Its edge pixels are 0% neutral, but the outline is not a clear dark material tone; it is a flat blue-ish contour, and the whole piece looks like a sticker. It is much less rich than the references.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny blue glyph of about 10 distinct colours, roughly 14x12 px. It reads as an abstract shape rather than a fallen chair: no legs, seat or backrest can be made out. It has about 2-3 lightness steps, a light blue top face and a darker blue underside. Its outline is a dark blue tint, not neutral, which agrees with the 0% neutral edge share. The measured facts show 0 visible tones per tile because the piece is smaller than a tile, so I judged density by eye. Beside the references it looks much thinner and flatter. The bench has a clear plank structure with highlights and grain. The well and stall carry many tones, stone-by-stone shading and per-element highlights. The candidate has no grain, no texture dots and no material detail, so it looks like a sticker or icon next to them. A careful artist would not accept it beside the Beodeul props.
